history.heading: Settlement and the condominium
paragraphs: Vanuatu, a Y-shaped archipelago of about 80 islands in the South Pacific, was settled around 3,000 years ago by the Lapita people. Chief Roi Mata's Domain, a 17th-century chiefly site, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Portuguese navigator Pedro Fernandes de Queirós arrived in 1606, and James Cook named the islands the New Hebrides in 1774.

In the 19th century many ni-Vanuatu were recruited or kidnapped ("blackbirding") to work on plantations in Australia and Fiji. In 1906 Britain and France agreed to rule the islands jointly as a condominium, with two separate administrations, legal systems and police forces.

history.heading: Independence
paragraphs: Vanuatu became independent on 30 July 1980 under Father Walter Lini, after a short-lived secession attempt on Espiritu Santo (the "Coconut War"). Cyclone Pam devastated the country in 2015, and a powerful earthquake struck Port Vila in December 2024.

culture.heading: Kastom
paragraphs: Vanuatu has over 100 indigenous languages, the highest density of languages per person in the world. Bislama, an English-based creole, is the national language, and English and French are also official. Most people are Christian, and the John Frum cargo cult exists on Tanna.

Kastom (traditional custom) remains strong. The land diving (Naghol) on Pentecost Island, in which men jump from towers with vines tied to their ankles, inspired bungee jumping. Kava is a central ceremonial drink.

politics.heading: Parliamentary republic
paragraphs: Vanuatu is a parliamentary republic with a president as head of state and a prime minister. Politics is fragmented, with frequent changes of government. A National Council of Chiefs advises on custom. Vanuatu led the campaign for an International Court of Justice advisory opinion on climate change, delivered in 2025.

economy.heading: Agriculture and tourism
paragraphs: Most people depend on subsistence farming. Exports include copra, kava, beef and cocoa. Tourism and a citizenship-by-investment programme are significant sources of revenue. Vanuatu is among the countries most exposed to natural disasters. The currency is the vatu.
